english.title: Fail to give information/assistance to person acting in the execution of the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable cause, failed to give to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person acting in the execution of the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006,

(A)_[assistance,]_
(B)_[information,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ASSISTANCE / INFORMATION..), reasonably required for the performance of that person's functions under those regulations
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 15(1)(b) and 17(3) of the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: The "Hygiene Regulations" ("y Rheoliadau Hylendid") means the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006 and the Community Regulations

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
